title: Not good to be alone (Genesis 2:18–25)
hook: the first thing the Torah calls "not good" is loneliness

segments.voice: Yesterday: adam, the earthling, shaped from dust and given breath. Your line was earth and breath. Which pocket did you reach into? Day twenty-seven.

So far, everything in this story has been good. Light, good. Land, good. Sun and moon, fish and birds, good. At the end of the sixth day, very good. Seven times we heard it, back on day six. Then, in the second chapter, there's the human, alone in the garden. Plenty to eat. Nothing dangerous. Nothing wrong at all, you'd think. And for the first time in the whole Torah, God looks at something and says it's not good. Not a sin. Not a monster. Not a flood. Something you might feel on a Sunday afternoon with your phone in your hand. Today: the first not good.
screen: `GOOD, GOOD, VERY GOOD.` → `A HUMAN, ALONE IN A GARDEN.` → `THE FIRST NOT GOOD.`

segments.voice: In the Jewish Publication Society's 1917 translation: "It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him a help meet for him." The first not good is loneliness. Now, that old phrase, help meet. It's often heard as a helper, an assistant. The Hebrew is ezer kenegdo. Ezer means help, and the Bible also uses that word for God. The Psalms say, in the same translation, "My help cometh from the LORD." That's ezer. It's not a junior word. And kenegdo means opposite him, facing him. Readers hear an equal in it: someone who can look you in the eye. Rashi noticed that kenegdo can also mean against him, and he gave a wry answer: if you're worthy, a help; if not, someone who pushes back. Then, in the story, the animals come. The human names each one, and none of them is the one. Something is still missing. The human sleeps, and a second person is made from the first, from the side, the text says. And the first human speaks the Torah's first human words, almost a song: "This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh." At last. The rabbis extended the idea far beyond marriage. There's a story in the Talmud about Honi, a man who slept for seventy years, woke up, and found that nobody knew him anymore. The Talmud closes his story with a saying people used: either companionship, or death. Friendship, study partners, community, family. People need people, and the Torah says it right at the start, before anything else goes wrong.
screen: `THE FIRST NOT GOOD: ALONE.` · `EZER — THE WORD USED FOR GOD.` · `KENEGDO — FACING, AS AN EQUAL.` · `BONE OF MY BONES.` · then, large: `EITHER COMPANIONSHIP, OR DEATH.`

segments.voice: Two minutes, with the bell. Think of someone who might be lonely right now. An older neighbor. A friend who moved away. A coworker who eats lunch by themselves. Someone who went quiet in the group chat. Picture their face. Then decide exactly what you'll send them: not a long message, just a real one. Hold it until the bell ends. The bell holds the time.
Not good to be alone. The first thing in the Torah called not good, and the help that faces you as an equal.
screen: `NOT GOOD TO BE ALONE — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: not good alone. Today, send the note you chose to the person who might be lonely. Then notice whether you feel a little less alone too. Day twenty-seven.

screen: `DAY 27 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: THE GARDEN AND THE QUESTION.`

howItsDone: Jewish tradition treats companionship as a basic need: study is often done in pairs, called chavruta, many prayers are said in community, and visiting the sick is counted a mitzvah.

trapdoor: what you thought: God makes Adam a wife.
what it means: the first thing called not good is loneliness, and the answer is someone who faces you as an equal.
what a scholar hears: ezer is used of God (Psalm 121:2); Rashi reads kenegdo as help or opposition; Honi's 'companionship or death' (Taanit 23a) widens it to all human bonds.

Word is the outline title's head ('Not good to be alone'), kept exactly.
'The first human words' of the Torah (2:23) — the human names animals in 2:20 without direct speech; confirm the claim.
